items.t: Canadian Pacific Kansas City (TSX:CP) Stock Could Be Above Fair Value As Merger Debate Heats Up
sum: Canadian Pacific Kansas City has been a strong performer in recent years, and the stock's climb puts fresh attention on whether the cash it can generate really backs up today's price. With the market reacting to both operational updates and industry merger debates, the key issue for you is how that share performance lines up with the cash flows the railway can produce over time.
Over the past 5 years, Canadian Pacific Kansas City has returned 47.3%, which puts a lot of expectation into the current valuation debate around its future cash generation.

Recent gains in revenue and earnings alongside higher fuel costs show how sensitive the business can be to both volume growth and input prices, which feeds directly into the amount of cash available for reinvestment or potential shareholder returns.
The issue now is whether that recent share price strength is adequately supported by the intrinsic value suggested by Canadian Pacific Kansas City's cash flows.
If you are weighing Canadian Pacific Kansas City against other opportunities that also hinge on cash generation, it can help to compare it with 6 high quality undervalued stocks.

The Discounted Cash Flow (DCF) model here focuses on what Canadian Pacific Kansas City can return to shareholders through future free cash flows. Latest twelve month free cash flow sits around CA$2.7b, and the forecasts used in this 2 Stage Free Cash Flow to Equity approach assume those cash flows grow from that base rather than shrink.

Projected figures step up into the CA$4b to CA$5b range over the coming decade, then settle into more measured increases, which is closer to a mature railway steadily adding capacity rather than a hyper growth story. Because the Discounted Cash Flow (DCF) outcome sits meaningfully below the current CA$134.18 share price, the current valuation leans more on qualitative factors such as network reach and potential merger ripple effects instead of the cash flow math alone. The strong Q3 revenue and earnings result that followed higher fuel costs helps explain why investors have been willing to pay above what the cash flow model supports. sum: Компания Canadian Pacific Kansas City сообщила во вторник, 3 ноября, что установила новые октябрьские рекорды по транспортировке зерна и зернопродуктов как в Канаде, так и в США. В сообщении, опубликованном на ее веб-сайте по связям с инвесторами, компания сообщила, что совокупный общий объем продаж в Канаде и США достиг рекордного месячного максимума по метрическим тоннам и вагонам.

В Канаде компания CPKC в октябре перевезла 3,26 миллиона метрических тонн и 33 822 вагона. Компания заявила, что это был третий рекордный месяц подряд в начале 2026-2027 сельскохозяйственного года, и он превысил предыдущий октябрьский максимум 2022 года. За 13-ю неделю поставки канадского зерна превысили 8,5 миллионов метрических тонн и составили 88 064 вагона.

Поставки зерна в США достигли 2,65 миллиона метрических тонн и 27 739 вагонов, побив предыдущий октябрьский рекорд 2024 года. CPKC сообщила, что ежемесячные рекорды по зерну в США были достигнуты в пяти из последних шести месяцев: мае, июне, июле, сентябре и октябре. В пресс-релизе не приводятся данные о выручке или прибыли от зерновой деятельности, поэтому показатели объемов остаются самым четким сигналом для инвесторов из обновленной информации.

Исполнительный вице-президент и директор по маркетингу Джон Брукс объяснил такие результаты еще одним урожаем в Северной Америке, превышающим средний уровень, а также сетью CPKC, охватывающей три страны, связывающей клиентов с глобальными рынками. Он сказал, что сеть способна поддержать еще один успешный зерновой сезон, сохраняя при этом надежное обслуживание по всей цепочке поставок.

Это сообщение имеет значение, поскольку объемы зерна являются индикатором спроса на грузоперевозки, но более высокий тоннаж не приводит автоматически к более высокой прибыли. Инвесторам по-прежнему необходимо взвешивать цены, затраты на обслуживание, топливо, рабочую силу и эффективность сети при оценке того, какая часть импульса объема достигает прибыли.

В обзоре инвесторов CPKC указан доход в третьем квартале 2026 года в размере 4,219 миллиарда канадских долларов, что на 15 процентов больше, чем в прошлом году, а операционная прибыль составила 1,487 миллиарда канадских долларов, что на 11 процентов больше. Базовая скорректированная операционная прибыль выросла на 12 процентов до 1,608 миллиарда канадских долларов, а базовая скорректированная разводненная прибыль на акцию увеличилась на 16 процентов до 1,28 канадских долларов. Сообщаемый операционный коэффициент составил 64,8 процента, при этом базовый скорректированный коэффициент составил 61,9 процента.

items.t: Current Landing to Host Official Kansas City Current Watch Party on Sunday
sum: KANSAS CITY (Nov. 12, 2026) — The No. 4 seed Kansas City Current will face top-seeded Gotham FC in the semifinals of the 2026 NWSL Playoffs, presented by Google Pixel, on Sunday, Nov. 15. Kickoff is set for 2 p.m. CT at Icahn Stadium on Randall’s Island in Manhattan, N.Y., with live coverage on ABC.

Current Landing, the district outside of CPKC Stadium, will be hosting the official watch party this Sunday, inviting fans to come together to support the team as it competes for a place in the championship match. The semifinal match will be played live on the big screen.

Tickets to the watch party are free and can be reserved here. Gates open at 1 p.m. CT. Fans can expect “Teal Time” themed photo opportunities with movie clappers, players’ names in Hollywood stars along the pavement and playoff vinyl on Helzberg Gate.

Fans are encouraged to arrive early to snag a Teal Time bracelet and free popcorn in themed Current boxes. Current branded tattoos will be available, plus fans can enjoy games like Plinko and Memory Match to earn prizes. There will be plenty of kid-friendly activities with an inflatable bounce house and sign-making station.
Along with live music by DJ Ness, fans can catch the pre-show and post-show coverage taking place at the KC Current Studios in Current Landing.

Recently opened restaurants, Providence Pizza and Revel at Current Landing will be open during the match, as well as the Pitchside trailer. Guests can order carryout from these restaurants while watching the match in Current Landing. Additional food and beverage can be purchased at the Current Landing concession stand. No other outside food and beverage will be allowed.
The 2026 NWSL Championship, presented by Google Pixel, is scheduled for Saturday, Nov. 21, at Audi Field in Washington, D.C., and will air live on CBS and Paramount+.

Canadian Pacific Kansas City stock gains freight momentum from grain records
sum: Canadian Pacific Kansas City reported a fresh operating milestone on November 3, 2026, as grain shipments reached monthly records across Canada and the United States. The company said the figures support the importance of its cross-border freight network, while the earnings outlook remains tied to broader operating execution.

CPKC investor relations reported that the railway moved 3.26 million metric tonnes and 33,822 carloads of grain and grain products in Canada during October. That marked the third consecutive record month at the start of the 2026-2027 crop year and exceeded the previous October record from 2022.

In the United States, CPKC transported 2.65 million metric tonnes and 27,739 carloads. The monthly total surpassed the previous U.S. October record from 2024. The company also said U.S. grain records were set in five of the past six months: May, June, July, September and October.

Combined Canadian and U.S. shipments reached all-time monthly records for both tonnage and carloads. For investors, the figures point to network utilization and freight demand rather than directly changing the earnings outlook. The key question is whether stronger throughput can translate into durable pricing, margins and cash generation.

The proposed development aimed to turn the Berkley Riverfront into a larger sports and entertainment destination. Plans included additional seating at CPKC Stadium, new restaurants, improved walking and cycling trails, a parking garage and a pedestrian bridge linking the River Market to the stadium.

New designs released by the Kansas City Current and architecture firm Gensler on June 30 offered a glimpse of how the district could change. The bridge, in particular, drew interest from people who regularly travel through the area.

Tori Carter, who works nearby, welcomed the idea of separating pedestrian movement from road traffic. “A bridge would be so big — it’s kind of just annoying when you’re driving and you’ve got to wait for people crossing, so a bridge would be huge,” Carter said.

Some residents also viewed the expansion as a natural next step for a neighbourhood that has changed significantly since the stadium opened. Azealia Dixon, who had lived in the area for three years, said the project could bring more activities and visitors to the city.

“I think it’s awesome. It brings a lot of people to Kansas City — more expansion, more fun, more things to do. And it’s local too and it’s convenient now so everyone kind of has the opportunity to come,” Dixon said.

CPKC Holiday Train returns to Texarkana Nov. 29 with free concert
sum: The CPKC Holiday Train is coming back to Texarkana. The lighted train will stop at the West 4th Street railway crossing in Texarkana, Texas, on Sunday, Nov. 29, for a free 30-minute show from 4:45 to 5:15 p.m.

Canadian band Magic!, known for the 2014 hit “Rude,” and singer-songwriter MARIS will perform from the train’s stage car. Each stop also includes a short presentation with local food bank representatives.

The show is free, but Canadian Pacific Kansas City asks visitors to bring a non-perishable food item or a cash donation. The railroad says every contribution stays in the community where it is collected.
Since 1999, the Holiday Train program has collected more than $28.3 million and over 5.6 million pounds of food for food banks in Canada and the U.S., according to CPKC.
Texarkana is one of three stops on Nov. 29. If you can’t make the Texarkana show, the train will also stop at these nearby locations:

Union Pacific releases video of CEO’s rate remarks at shipper conference
sum: OMAHA, Neb. — Union Pacific today released its video of CEO Jim Vena’s March shipper association speech, which includes his controversial remarks about raising rates for customers who opposed the UP-Norfolk Southern merger.

Vena touted the benefits of the merger during the 52-minute, 42-second video. At the end of the recording of the keynote address at the Southwest Association of Rail Shippers meeting, Vena said: “So bottom line is we’re going to get this done. It’s good for the country, good for our employees, and it’s good for all of you if you actually sit back and take a look at what we’re going to be able to offer. We’re willing to make deals with customers. So come and see us. Talk about what you need to move ahead with us and how we put this thing forward. If we don’t do that, Union Pacific will still be there. And if I stick around, which I probably will, I’ll probably increase everybody’s rates that said they didn’t want a seamless railroad by three or four extra percent to teach you a lesson. Thank you very much.”
The CEO then waved and walked offscreen at the end of the question-and-answer session.

The remarks prompted Sen. Tammy Baldwin (D-Wis.) to write to the Surface Transportation Board in July to express concerns that UP was threatening to retaliate against shippers who didn’t back the merger. CPKC and a coalition of shipper groups subsequently sought to have the UP video made public as part of the merger review. And last week CPKC urged the STB to toss out the UP-NS merger application, arguing that Vena’s comments have made it impossible for regulators to develop a full evidentiary record because shippers are afraid to speak out.

The STB on Wednesday rejected UP’s appeal of an administrative law judge’s order to make the video public, ruling that the appeal was late and lacked merit. The board ordered UP to remove the video’s confidential designation and provide it to all parties by 5 p.m. Eastern today.
In a statement accompanying the video, UP sought to put the remarks into the context of the entire speech and encouraged shippers to participate in the merger review process.

items.t: Canadian singer-songwriter Tyler Shaw looking to secure spot in ‘world’s biggest live music event’
sum: A Canadian artist set to perform in Simcoe County is vying for a spot in an international music contest. Singer-songwriter Tyler Shaw, known for hits like “House of Cards,” “To the Man Who Let Her Go” and “With You,” is one of five Canadian artists who are contenders to represent Canada at the Eurovision Song Contest 2027. Hosted by the European Broadcasting Union,Eurovision is touted as “the world’s biggest live music event” where artists from around the world compete in the singing competition. The winner will receive a glass microphone trophy and their country will get the honour of hosting the event the following year. “It’s the Olympics of songwriting essentially,” Shaw tells CTV News in an exclusive interview. The competition not only puts a spotlight on the Canadian arts scene, but Shaw says this is a huge opportunity for him as it could give him the global recognition he’s looking for. “It opens up a lot of doors for artists here in Canada especially with this contest,” Shaw says. Members of the public can vote with Thursday being the last day. CPKC Holiday Train Not only is Shaw gearing up for Eurovision, but he’s also set to perform in our region on the CPKC Holiday Train. It’s making a whopping 50 stops. Once the train rolls in, an entire side of one of the cars folds down and transforms into a makeshift stage. He’s set to perform for around 15 minutes. Whether there are a handful of people or thousands gathered, Shaw says the energy is high. “When that happens, you just can’t stop the excitement, no matter how big or small the crowd is,” Shaw says. Shaw released his first album in 2015 and since then, he says if you pay attention to life, you can find inspiration everywhere. “The inspiration, it really does just follow my life,” Shaw says. But the last few years have especially given him something to write about. “Obviously becoming a father has opened up perspective over the last six years and just story-telling wise,” Shaw says. Shaw’s forthcoming album there’s no easy way to put this... will be out Feb. 19. The title track was released at the end of last month. The train will roll up in Springwater, MacTier and Parry Sound on Nov. 30.

Canadian Pacific Kansas City stock posts 15% Q3 revenue growth
sum: Canadian Pacific Kansas City reported third-quarter revenue of 4.219 billion Canadian dollars on October 28, up 15 percent from the same period a year earlier. The release from CPKC investor relations showed a mixed quarter: volumes improved, but fuel inflation pushed operating ratios higher.

Revenue ton-miles rose 6 percent in the three months ended September 30. Freight revenue reached 4.139 billion Canadian dollars, with grain revenue increasing to 904 million Canadian dollars from 702 million a year earlier and intermodal revenue rising to 815 million Canadian dollars from 668 million.

Reported operating expenses climbed to 2.732 billion Canadian dollars from 2.325 billion. Fuel expense was 667 million Canadian dollars, compared with 415 million in the prior-year quarter. The reported operating ratio increased to 64.8 percent from 63.5 percent, while the core adjusted ratio rose to 61.9 percent from 60.7 percent.

CPKC said higher fuel prices affected the reported and core adjusted operating ratios by 170 and 190 basis points, respectively. The company also reported diluted earnings per share of 1.04 Canadian dollars, compared with 1.01 Canadian dollars a year earlier. Core adjusted diluted earnings per share rose to 1.28 Canadian dollars from 1.10 Canadian dollars.

Net income was 916 million Canadian dollars, nearly unchanged from 917 million in the third quarter of 2025. The reported result included acquisition-related and other discrete tax items, including a 94 million Canadian dollar reassessment related to the Kansas City Southern acquisition. CPKC's adjusted figures exclude specified items and are not standardized under generally accepted accounting principles.

Chief Executive Officer Keith Creel said the railroad was running well and that service remained strong across grain, intermodal and merchandise markets. He said disciplined execution and the company's North American network kept CPKC on track to meet its commitments for 2026.

The company retained its full-year targets for low-double-digit growth in core adjusted diluted earnings per share and mid-single-digit growth in revenue ton-miles. Capital spending is planned at approximately 2.65 billion Canadian dollars.

sum: Canadian Pacific Kansas City reported strong third-quarter growth on October 28, but higher fuel costs kept pressure on operating efficiency. In its earnings release, the railroad said revenue reached CAD 4.219 billion in the three months ended September 30, up 15 percent from CAD 3.661 billion a year earlier.

Volume, measured in revenue ton-miles, increased 6 percent. Reported diluted earnings per share rose 3 percent to CAD 1.04 from CAD 1.01, while core adjusted diluted earnings per share climbed 16 percent to CAD 1.28 from CAD 1.10. The adjusted figure is a non-GAAP measure and is therefore not directly comparable with every company reporting under standard accounting definitions.

The main pressure point was the operating ratio, where a lower percentage indicates better efficiency. CPKC's reported ratio increased to 64.8 percent from 63.5 percent, while the core adjusted ratio rose to 61.9 percent from 60.7 percent. The company said higher fuel prices affected the reported ratio by 170 basis points and the core adjusted ratio by 190 basis points.

Operating income nevertheless increased 11 percent to CAD 1.487 billion from CAD 1.336 billion. The company also reported freight revenue of CAD 4.139 billion, compared with CAD 3.589 billion in the third quarter of 2025. Grain and intermodal were among the growth areas highlighted by management, supporting the case that network expansion and pricing are offsetting part of the cost pressure.

sum: Canadian Pacific Kansas City reported stronger revenue and adjusted earnings for the third quarter on October 28, while higher fuel costs put pressure on operating efficiency. The company said it remains on track to meet its commitments for 2026.

According to the CPKC earnings release, revenue rose 15 percent year over year to CAD 4.219 billion in the three months ended September 30, from CAD 3.661 billion a year earlier. Revenue ton-miles increased 6 percent, with freight revenue reaching CAD 4.139 billion.

Reported operating income increased to CAD 1.487 billion from CAD 1.336 billion. Reported diluted earnings per share rose 3 percent to CAD 1.04 from CAD 1.01. Core adjusted diluted EPS, a non-GAAP measure, increased 16 percent to CAD 1.28 from CAD 1.10.

The improvement in adjusted earnings came despite a sharper cost burden. CPKC's reported operating ratio rose to 64.8 percent from 63.5 percent, while the core adjusted ratio increased to 61.9 percent from 60.7 percent. The company said higher fuel prices affected the reported ratio by 170 basis points and the core adjusted ratio by 190 basis points.

Fuel expense climbed to CAD 667 million from CAD 415 million in the prior-year quarter. Net income attributable to controlling shareholders was CAD 917 million, compared with CAD 920 million a year earlier. The financial statements also show quarterly operating cash flow of CAD 1.550 billion, up from CAD 1.274 billion.

Chief Executive Officer Keith Creel said the railroad continued to grow in grain, intermodal and merchandise markets. He pointed to disciplined execution and a robust commercial pipeline as reasons for maintaining confidence in the company's full-year commitments.

Management expects mid-single-digit growth in revenue ton-miles for 2026 and continues to target low double-digit growth in core adjusted diluted EPS. Capital spending is expected to total approximately CAD 2.65 billion for the year. The company also expects a fourth-quarter operating ratio below 60 percent, supported by October volumes, network performance and a favorable weather outlook.

CPKC net income falls despite rising revenues
sum: CALGARY, ALBERTA, CANADA —– Canadian Pacific Kansas City Railway (CPKC) on July 29 posted a decline in net income in the second quarter of 2026 despite a sharp increase in revenues.

Net income decreased 17% to C$1.02 billion in the April-June quarter compared with the same period in 2025. Meanwhile, revenues soared by 13% year on year to C$4.16 billion due to a bumper Canadian grain crop. The company’s grain transportation revenue rose by nearly 25% compared with the same period last year.

Grain freight revenue per revenue ton-mile rose from C$4.96 in the second quarter of 2025 to C$5.19 in the same quarter this year. The company transported 168,000 carloads of grain in the second quarter compared with 142,000 in the same period in 2025.

CPKC earlier this month announced that it had set a new June monthly record for transporting Canadian grain and grain products, moving 2.8 million tonnes. It beat the previous tonnage record set in June 2020. CPKC also set a second-quarter record for tonnage and carloads.

CPKC said operating ratio increased by 90 basis points to 64.6% from 63.7% in the second quarter of 2025, while core adjusted operating ratio increased 90 basis points to 61.6% from 60.7% in the previous year’s second quarter
Reported diluted EPS decreased 14% to $1.15, while core adjusted diluted EPS increased 13% to $1.27 year on year, beating the consensus estimate of $1.24.

Keith Creel, president and chief executive officer of CPKC, told analysts during a conference call that the company has benefited from being the only North American railway to span all three countries — Canada, the United States and Mexico.

Canadian Pacific Kansas City Limited declares dividend
sum: CALGARY, AB, July 29, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- The Board of Directors of Canadian Pacific Kansas City Limited (TSX: CP) (NYSE: CP) (CPKC) today declared a quarterly dividend of $0.268 per share on the outstanding Common Shares.

The dividend is payable on October 26, 2026, to holders of record at the close of business on September 25, 2026, and is an "eligible" dividend for purposes of the Income Tax Act (Canada) and any similar provincial/territorial legislation.

With its global headquarters in Calgary, Alta., Canada, CPKC is the first and only single-line transnational railway linking Canada, the United States and México, with unrivaled access to major ports from Vancouver to Atlantic Canada to the Gulf Coast to Lázaro Cárdenas, México. Stretching approximately 20,000 route miles and employing approximately 20,000 railroaders, CPKC provides North American customers unparalleled rail service and network reach to key markets across the continent. CPKC is growing with its customers, offering a suite of freight transportation services, logistics solutions and supply chain expertise. Visit cpkcr.com to learn more about the rail advantages of CPKC. CP-IR

items.t: Freight train struck a person on CPKC tracks
sum: DRYDEN — Ontario Provincial Police and the Office of the Chief Coroner are investigating a recent fatality on a railway line in Dryden.
A man was pronounced deceased after a collision with a CPKC train last week.

"I can share that on Tuesday, June 9 just after 7 a.m., a CPKC train made contact with a person on the tracks near Sandy Beach Road in Dryden, Ont.," a railway spokesperson wrote in an email to Newswatch.
OPP initially announced on the morning of June 9 that two local rail crossings were blocked by a train due to an ongoing investigation, and advised motorists to avoid the area.
They said updates would be provided later, but subsequently referred news reporters to CPKC, saying the incident was under the jurisdiction of railway police.
This week, OPP said their involvement has changed since then, and that they are conducting an investigation into what was described as a "non-suspicious" fatality.
The Transportation Safety Board of Canada reports that it is aware of the occurrence, but that its role is limited to gathering data for statistical reporting and future analysis.

Kansas City Current, BofA Announces Multi-Year Partnership Renewal Featuring Enhanced Community Efforts
sum: KANSAS CITY (June 16, 2026) — The Kansas City Current and Bank of America announced a multi-year partnership renewal on Tuesday, set to celebrate community impact and grow the game of soccer nationwide. Bank of America will continue being an official partner of the club as part of the announcement, and the Current will support Bank of America’s landmark global sports program, Sports with Us.

Tuesday’s announcement reaffirms Bank of America’s longstanding commitment to the Current both on and off the pitch. A partner of the Current since 2023, Bank of America and the Current will lead several impactful initiatives throughout the duration of the renewed partnership.

Bank of America has collaborated with the Current on several community initiatives over the last three years. Bank of America frequently serves as a presenting sponsor of KC Current youth soccer clinics, including a combined clinic and equipment donation drive last summer at the 9th & Van Brunt Athletic Fields.

“Renewing our partnership with a world-class, globally known brand like Bank of America represents a significant milestone for our organization,” said Kansas City Current Senior Vice President, Commercial Missy Jenkins. “Their steadfast support over the last three years has been extremely meaningful, and we greatly appreciate their continued belief in what we are building here in Kansas City. Our shared community pillars and commitment to youth sports will continue making this partnership resonate across the Heartland.”

The Current will also partner with Bank of America to help bring select “Soccer With Us” clinics to life — free, hands-on soccer experiences reaching underserved communities —designed to equip the next generation for success on and off the pitch.

Bank of America maintains a strong regional footprint across the Kansas City area. With 33 locations across the Kansas City metro, Bank of America invests locally to ensure Kansas City is a great place to live, work and do business. Bank of America is also the Official Bank of FIFA World Cup 2026 ™ — supporting all 106 matches across North America — making a huge economic impact and inspiring the next generation of soccer players.

items.t: Royal Ottawa to host Brooke Henderson and CPKC Women's Open in 2027
sum: Brooke Henderson will have another chance to be a hero in her hometown next summer.
Golf Canada and Canadian Pacific Kansas City (CPKC) announced on Monday afternoon that the prestigious Royal Ottawa Golf Club in Gatineau will host the 2027 CPKC Women’s Open from August 18-22, 2027.

Henderson, 28, a native of nearby Smiths Falls, will defend the second CPKC championship she won last year at the Mississauga Golf and Country Club last summer at the 2026 women’s open being held in August at the Royal Mayfair Golf Club in Edmonton.
The 2027 tournament will be back at the Royal Ottawa for the second time in its 53-year history after previously hosting the event in 2000.
This will be the tournament’s sixth appearance in the Ottawa-Gatineau region, the previous being in 2022 when it was held at the Ottawa Hunt and Golf Club.
The event at the Hunt was one of the most successful in the history of the tourney.

“The National Capital region historically has been a tremendous host to the CPKC Women’s Open with wonderful fans coming out in big numbers for this incredible event and its critical mission supporting local heart charities that make such a difference in their communities,” CPKC president and CEO Keith Creel said.

CPKC says its coal segment weighed on Q1 results, record grain volumes a bright spot
sum: Canadian Pacific Kansas City Ltd.'s coal segment weighed on its first-quarter results even as the company benefited from record grain volumes.

"We definitely weren't counting on the drag related to the coal side of the business. Now looking ahead, just about everything outside of our coal business has inflected positive," said John Brooks, executive vice-president and chief marketing officer at CPKC.

Freight revenues for the company's coal segment fell 12 percent compared to the previous year, coming in at $226 million. The Calgary-based company expects coal to continue to be a headwind going forward.

CPKC reported net income of $845 million during the first quarter, down from $909 million during the same period last year. That amounted to diluted earnings per share of 94 cents during the three months ended March 31, down from 97 cents during the prior-year quarter.
CPKC says its revenue was $3.7 billion during the quarter, down year-over-year from $3.8 billion.
Freight revenues from CPKC's grain segment rose by 11 per cent, reaching $871 million.

"We delivered solid volume growth across the network, led by record grain and continued momentum from our unique North American footprint. The exceptional grain volumes were supported by record harvest and our ability to efficiently connect Canada to the United States and Mexico," Keith Creel, the CEO of CPKC, said on the company's earnings call.

CPKC announces 135-unit locomotive order, divided between Progress Rail and Wabtec
sum: CALGARY, Alberta — CPKC has ordered 65 new EMD SD70ACe-T4 Tier 4 locomotives from Progress Rail and 70 Wabtec Evolution Series ET44AC Tier 4 locomotives as part of the railway’s $800 million, multiyear fleet renewal program.

The SD70ACe-T4s, which will be manufactured at the Progress Rail facility in Muncie, Ind., feature a new energy management system that improves fuel efficiency by 5% to 7% over prior first generation Tier 4 units, while continuing to meet EPA Tier 4 emissions standards without after-treatment.

“We are pleased to make this significant investment in American manufacturing with Progress Rail,” CPKC Chief Operating Officer Mark Redd said. “The purchase of these units continues CPKC’s locomotive renewal program to accommodate future growth, increase fleet reliability, and decrease emissions as we safely and efficiently serve our customers and the North American economy.”

The locomotives will feature Progress Rail’s Talos energy management system, certified by the EPA to deliver a 12.3% efficiency gain, which Progress said is industry-leading benchmark for fuel savings and reduced emissions. Powered by artificial intelligence, Talos optimizes in-train forces and has logged over four million miles without a break-in-two.

“We’re proud to partner with CPKC to introduce our updated Tier 4 platform,” said Progress Rail CEO John Newman. “After years of investment to enhance reliability and fuel efficiency and months of rigorous testing by CPKC in some of North America’s most rugged operating environments, these locomotives are prepared to deliver the performance our Class I railroad customers demand. This milestone reflects our commitment to innovation and delivering real solutions to solve our customer’s toughest challenges.”
With 4,500 brake horsepower and up to 200,000 lbs. of starting tractive effort, the SD70ACe-T4 allows railroads to move longer, heavier trains with fewer locomotives, Progress Rail said.
Thirty of the locomotives will be delivered in the second half of 2026, CPKC said.

items.t: CPKC profits rise as economy, trade issues drag freight
sum: Canadian Pacific Kansas City on Wednesday reported higher fourth-quarter profits on freight volumes that narrowly improved.

“Our story is about continuing to do what we do best: Controlling what we can control, and executing our PSR model, which remains key to setting CPKC (NYSE: CP) apart and allows us to shine in times of uncertainty,” Chief Executive Keith Creel said on the railway’s earnings call, referring to the Precision Scheduled Railroading operating model. “We saw that in the results in the last quarter. We’ll continue to see that in 2026.”
For the quarter, operating income grew 3%, to US$1.19 billion, as revenue increased 1%, to $2.89 billion. Earnings per share, adjusted for the impact of one-time items, increased 3%, to 98 cents.
Quarterly expenses were flat. The railway’s 58.9% operating ratio set a quarterly record for CPKC and was a 0.8-point improvement compared to the fourth quarter of 2024.

Fourth-quarter volume was flat on the basis of revenue ton-miles but up 1% when measured by carloads and intermodal containers. On a carload basis, coal and intermodal were the only business segments to see growth. Grain and potash carloads were flat, while CPKC’s remaining business segments declined.

Chief Marketing Officer John Brooks said that U.S. tariffs continue to weigh on CPKC’s Canadian forest products traffic as well as cross-border steel shipments. The railway is counting on forecast bumper grain crops in Canada and the U.S. to boost volumes this year.
The railway’s Mexico Midwest Express flagship intermodal service, which links Chicago with points in Mexico, continues to grow, with volume up 40% year-over-year in the fourth quarter, Brooks said.

items.t: Kansas City Current Announces Chris Armas as Head Coach
sum: KANSAS CITY (Jan. 7, 2026) – The Kansas City Current has appointed Chris Armas as the club’s head coach, the organization announced Wednesday. Armas, who was inducted into the National Soccer Hall of Fame in 2025, has over three decades of playing and coaching experience at the highest level of the sport.

“We are beyond excited to welcome Chris to the Kansas City Current family,” said co-owners Angie and Chris Long. “He brings an abundance of experience at the highest levels both as a coach and a player and shares in our long-term vision of the Kansas City Current being the best women’s football club in the world. A natural leader, Chris demands excellence, and we are confident he will further cultivate and enhance our competitive environment as we continue to pursue championships and expand our global footprint.”

Most recently, Armas was the head coach of the Colorado Rapids in Major League Soccer (MLS) during the 2024 and 2025 seasons. He led the Rapids back to the Audi MLS Cup Playoffs in 2024 and earned a third-place finish in the 2025 Leagues Cup while capturing back-to-back Rocky Mountain Cup titles.

Armas’ coaching career began in 2008 as an assistant for Chicago Fire FC before spending four years as the head women’s soccer coach at Adelphi University, his alma mater, from 2011-14. Under his direction, Adelphi had back-to-back Northeast 10 (NE10) Tournament final appearances in 2012 and 2013, earned its first NCAA Tournament berth in six years in 2013 and rose as high as ninth in the national rankings in 2014. Armas, who produced 20 All-Conference and six All-Region selections during his time with the Panthers, was recognized as the United Soccer Coaches Regional Coaching Staff of the Year and the NE10 Conference Coaching Staff of the Year in 2013.

In 2015, he joined the New York Red Bulls as an assistant coach and the team won the Supporters’ Shield that year. Armas was appointed the Red Bulls’ head coach in July 2018, finishing the regular season with a 12-3-3 record as the club won the 2018 Supporters’ Shield and advanced to the Eastern Conference Finals. He was then an assistant coach for Manchester United (2021-22) and Leeds United (2023) in the English Premier League, even serving as co-interim head coach of Leeds United.

Kansas City Current, Forward Amelia White Agree to Two-Year Contract Through 2027
sum: KANSAS CITY (Jan. 6, 2026) – Forward Amelia White, who recently concluded a four-year career at Penn State University, has signed her first professional contract with the Kansas City Current. White inked a two-year deal to keep her in Kansas City through the 2027 season, and she will join the team ahead of upcoming preseason training.

“We are thrilled to welcome Amelia to the Kansas City Current,” said general manager Ryan Dell. “Her professionalism, competitive drive and dedication to getting better each day make her a perfect fit for our culture. Amelia is riding a wave of momentum after a standout senior season at Penn State, and this is just the beginning for her. She will add depth to our attack and we are excited to help her continue to develop here in Kansas City.”

White started 53 of her 88 collegiate games with the Nittany Lions, logging nearly 4,500 career minutes and totaling 11 goals, 14 assists, 36 points and four game-winning goals. She amassed six goals and four assists as a senior in 2025 to double her previous single-season career high scoring mark en route to publishing a 16-point campaign, which ranked third on Penn State’s roster. Her career-best five assists came during her junior season.

The Fort Wayne, Ind. native had a team-high three game-winning goals in 2025 which ranked eighth in the Big Ten Conference. Two of those game-winners were in Big Ten regular season action. The forward also tallied a goal and an assist against Army in the first round of the 2025 NCAA Tournament for the first time in her career.

Her prolific senior campaign earned her a spot on the United Soccer Coaches All-Region Fourth Team as well as the All-Big Ten Second Team. White also landed on the All-Big Ten Freshman Team in 2022, the same year she helped lead the Nittany Lions to the Big Ten Tournament title. She was part of four NCAA Tournament squads as her team advanced to the national quarterfinals in 2023 and 2024.

“I’m incredibly excited to begin my professional career with the Kansas City Current,” said White. “This is a club with a clear vision, high standards and a competitive culture, and that’s exactly the kind of environment I want to be in.
